newsitem.title: USA: Alabama highway bond passes first legislative step.
newsitem.headline: Alabama highway bond passes first legislative step.

text.p: The $700 million revenue bond bill proposed by Gov. Fob James for highway construction was approved by the Joint Legislative Transportation Committee, an aide to the committee chairman said Friday.

Thursday's unanimous approval by the bipartisan committee was an administrative first step that formally sends the bill to the House and Senate for action, the aide said. The proposal is expected to face numerous amendments as it progresses through the various committees.
"It's got a long way to go," the aide said.
The proposal would use existing gasoline taxes to pay debt service on 20-year bonds.

It allocates $150 million for resurfacing roads and highways, $150 million for bridge repair and replacement, $81.9 million to be divided among the state's 67 counties for local projects, and $318 million for urban bypasses, lane additions and other specific projects.

Several lawmakers have already said they will challenge the way the money is distributed among counties, while others have suggested that the state wait to see how much transportation money it gets from Congress before issuing any highway bonds.
